function.name: generate_image_tool
function.description: Generates an image based on the provided description and saves it with the specified file name. The image description should be detailed to ensure the resulting image matches the desired subject and surroundings; otherwise, these aspects will be chosen randomly. This function is not intended for generating images from textual data. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

desc.description: A single string that provides a detailed description of the desired image. For example, 'a sunset over the mountains with a lake in the foreground'.

file_name.description: The name of the file to which the generated image will be saved. It should include the file extension, such as 'image.png'.

function.name: tts_tool
function.description: Converts the provided text content to speech and saves the resulting audio to a file. This function is intended for voice narration and should be used accordingly. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The text content that needs to be converted to speech.

speaker.description: The voice to be used for the text-to-speech conversion.

file_name.description: The name of the file to save the audio output without the extension. If left empty, a default name will be generated based on the content.

function.name: write_markdown_tool
function.description: Writes the provided content to a Markdown (.md) file on the disk. This function should be used when there is a need to persist text data in Markdown format as a result of a user action or a process that requires saving information in a structured text file. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The Markdown formatted text content to be written to the file.

filename.description: The name of the file to which the Markdown content will be written. If not provided, a default filename will be used.

function.name: write_html_tool
function.description: Writes an HTML file to disk with the given content. Ensures HTML tags within the content are properly closed. This function should be used when there is a need to save HTML content to a file as part of a 'save' operation. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The HTML content to be written to the file. Must contain valid HTML structure.

filename.description: The name of the file to which the HTML content will be written. If not provided, a default filename will be used.

function.name: search_web_tool
function.description: Executes a search query using the DuckDuckGo search engine and returns a specified number of search results from a given source. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

query.description: The search term or phrase to be queried.

num_results.description: The maximum number of search results to return. A positive integer.

source.description: The source from which the search results should be fetched.

function.name: get_url_content
function.description: Scrapes the specified URL for textual data and returns the content as a string. This function is useful for extracting information from web pages when a URL is provided. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The web address of the page to scrape. It should be a valid URL format, such as 'http://www.example.com'.

timeout.description: The maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, with a default value that allows for a reasonable amount of time for most web pages to load.

user_agent.description: The User-Agent string to be used for the HTTP request to simulate a particular browser, which is optional. Some websites may require this for access.

message.content:
Here’s a quick rundown of the most common tools, APIs, and platforms you can use to book flights (or at least find flight data and prices). I’ve grouped them into three categories: **flight‑search & booking APIs**, **aggregator / comparison sites**, and **flight‑tracking / data feeds**.

| Category | Tool / Service | What it offers | Typical use case |
|----------|----------------|----------------|------------------|
| **Flight‑search & booking APIs** | **Amadeus for Developers** | Full‑fledged flight search, booking, and itinerary management. Supports seat selection, e‑tickets, and ancillary services. | Building a custom travel app or integrating booking into your own platform. |
| | **Sabre APIs** | Comprehensive airline inventory, pricing, and booking. Includes seat maps, fare rules, and e‑ticket issuance. | Enterprise travel agencies, corporate booking portals. |
| | **Travelport Universal API** | Global distribution system (GDS) access to airlines, hotels, car rentals. | Multi‑service travel agencies, large‑scale booking engines. |
| | **Expedia Rapid API** | Search, price, and booking for flights, hotels, cars. | Integrating Expedia’s inventory into a third‑party site. |
| | **Skyscanner API** | Search, price alerts, and flight comparison. No direct booking – redirects to partner sites. | Price‑comparison widgets, flight‑price alert apps. |
| | **Kayak API** | Similar to Skyscanner – search and price comparison, no direct booking. | Embedding Kayak search into a website or app. |
| | **Priceline API** | Search and booking for flights, hotels, cars. | Building a Priceline‑powered booking experience. |
| | **CheapOair API** | Search, price, and booking. | Affiliate marketing or travel‑booking sites. |
| | **Skiplagged API** | Search for “hidden city” fares and cheaper itineraries. | Niche fare‑finding tools. |
| | **Aviationstack API** | Real‑time flight status, schedules, and airport data. | Flight‑status widgets, real‑time tracking. |
| | **FlightAware API** | Live flight tracking, historical data, and alerts. | Flight‑tracking dashboards, aviation analytics. |
| | **OpenSky Network API** | Open‑source flight‑track data. | Research, open‑data projects. |
| | **FlightStats API** | Flight status, delays, and historical performance. | Airline performance dashboards, travel insurance. |
| | **Google Flights API** *(unofficial)* | Not officially released, but some developers reverse‑engineer the data. | Experimental projects, data scraping. |
| | **Microsoft Bing Travel API** | Flight search and booking via Microsoft’s travel portal. | Integrating Bing’s travel data into apps. |
| | **TripIt API** | Aggregates itineraries from email confirmations. | Personal travel planners, itinerary managers. |
| | **Hopper API** *(private)* | Predictive pricing and booking. | Price‑prediction tools, travel recommendation engines. |
| | **Airline‑specific APIs** (e.g., Delta, United, Southwest) | Direct access to airline inventory and booking. | Airline‑branded booking widgets. |
| | **OpenTravel APIs** (e.g., OpenTravel Alliance) | Standardized travel data exchange. | Interoperability between travel tech vendors. |
| | **Booking.com API** | Hotel booking, not flights. | Complementary hotel booking in a travel app. |
| | **Airbnb API** | Accommodation, not flights. | Complementary lodging options. |
| | **Google Maps Places API** | Airport locations, nearby services. | Enhancing travel itineraries with local info. |
| | **FlightRadar24 API** | Live flight tracking. | Real‑time flight‑tracking widgets. |
| | **FlightAware Firehose** | Streaming flight data. | High‑frequency flight‑tracking applications. |
| | **OpenFlights API** | Airport, airline, route data. | Data enrichment for travel apps. |
| | **FlightLabs API** | Flight search and booking. | Alternative to major GDSs. |
| | **Travelport GDS** | Legacy GDS integration. | Traditional travel agency software. |

### How to pick the right tool

1. **Do you need a full booking flow?**  
   *Use a GDS‑based API (Amadeus, Sabre, Travelport) or a partner API that handles e‑ticket issuance (Expedia Rapid, Priceline, CheapOair).*

2. **Do you just need price comparison?**  
   *Use Skyscanner, Kayak, or Skyscanner Affiliate (if you want to earn commissions).*

3. **Do you want to embed flight‑status or live tracking?**  
   *Use FlightAware, FlightStats, Aviationstack, or FlightRadar24.*

4. **Do you want to offer airline‑branded booking widgets?**  
   *Many airlines provide their own APIs (Delta, United, Southwest, Air France, etc.).*

5. **Do you want to monetize traffic?**  
   *Affiliate programs (Skyscanner Affiliate, Travelpayouts, Expedia Affiliate Network) let you earn commissions on bookings made through your links.*

6. **Do you need research or open data?**  
   *OpenSky Network, OpenFlights, FlightLabs, or OpenTravel provide free or low‑cost data for analysis.*

---

### Quick start checklist

| Step | Action | Tool |
|------|--------|------|
| 1 | Sign up for an API key | Amadeus, Sabre, Travelport, Expedia Rapid, Skyscanner, Kayak, FlightAware, etc. |
| 2 | Read the documentation | Each provider has SDKs (Python, JavaScript, etc.) and sample code. |
| 3 | Test with sandbox / demo environment | Most GDSs have a sandbox; Skyscanner and Kayak provide test keys. |
| 4 | Build your UI | Use React/Vue for front‑end, Node/Python for back‑end. |
| 5 | Handle payment & e‑ticket issuance | If you’re issuing tickets, you’ll need a payment gateway (Stripe, PayPal) and compliance with airline regulations. |
| 6 | Deploy & monitor | Cloud hosting (AWS, Azure, GCP) + logging (Datadog, Sentry). |

---

### Bottom line

If you’re building a **full booking engine** (search → select → pay → e‑ticket), you’ll likely need a GDS‑based solution (Amadeus, Sabre, Travelport) or a partner that handles the ticketing step (Expedia Rapid, Priceline, CheapOair). If you’re only looking to **compare prices** or **embed flight‑search widgets**, Skyscanner, Kayak, or Skiplagged are great starting points. For **live flight status** or **tracking**, FlightAware, FlightStats, or Aviationstack are the industry standards. And if you want to **earn money** from referrals, affiliate APIs from Skyscanner, Travelpayouts, or Expedia are worth exploring.
